BritBox ‘s Agatha Christie series “Tommy & Tuppence” has found a home in the U.K. on Channel 5 .

The six-part drama will be available to stream and watch live this festive season, it was announced on Wednesday. Starring Antonia Thomas and Josh Dylan, the modern take on Christie's characters premiered on BritBox in North America Sept. 15.

“Tommy & Tuppence” also stars Imelda Staunton ("Harry Potter," "Paddington") as Tommy's Aunt Ada, Nicholas Richardson ("Wu-Tang: An American Saga," "Younger"), Charlie Condou ("Doctor Who," "Unforgotten"), Callie Cooke ("F1," "Cheaters") and Chizzy Akudolu ("Little Disasters," "The Woman in the Wall").

It was written and executive produced by Phoebe Eclair-Powell (“The Road Trip,” “Harm”) with Fergus O'Brien (“Happy Valley,” “The Tourist”) and Ellie Heydon (“Outrageous,” “Trying”) directing. Stella Merz (“Miss Austen,” “Gentleman Jack”) serves as producer. The show hails from Lookout Point, part of BBC Studios, and was produced in association with Agatha Christie Limited.

"'Agatha Christie's Tommy & Tuppence' brings together everything audiences love about a great mystery: clever plotting, intriguing characters and plenty of twists along the way,” said Cherry Vantreen, acquisitions and co-production director at 5. “With its charming central duo and blend of suspense, adventure and wit, it's a fantastic addition to 5's drama offering, and we're delighted to be bringing this classic Agatha Christie title to our viewers." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Added Eclair-Powell: "I'm so excited to see ‘Agatha Christie's Tommy & Tuppence' coming to Channel 5. Tommy and Tuppence are two of Christie's most entertaining and dynamic creations, and bringing their wit, warmth and sense of adventure to the screen has been an incredible experience. I'm delighted that new audiences will have the chance to discover their world of mystery, intrigue and romance."

The series was executive produced by Katie Draper, Louise Mutter, Laura Lankester and Juliette Howell for Lookout Point as well as Eclair-Powell and James Prichard for Agatha Christie Limited. BBC Studios struck the deal with 5 and is handling global sales.

articles.title: Rockstar Confirms GTA 6 Will Never Get a 60fps Mode on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S
articles.summary: Courtesy of Rockstar Games Players hoping to experience Grand Theft Auto 6 at 60 frames per second on current-generation consoles may need to adjust their expectations. Rockstar Games has made it clear that the highly anticipated open-world game is designed to run at 30fps on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, and a future update isn't going to change […]
articles.content:
As reported by IGN , Rockstar has confirmed that the PS5 Pro doesn't have the processing power necessary to run GTA 6 at 60fps. The console does offer a more capable graphics processor and improved upscaling technology compared to the standard PS5, but those advantages aren't enough to overcome the demands placed on its central processor. That limitation is particularly important for a game built around an enormous open world filled with complex systems and a densely populated environment.

The decision is consistent with Rockstar's previous confirmation that GTA 6 targets 30fps across current-generation consoles. The studio has emphasized that the game pushes the hardware to its limits, with its performance target allowing developers to maintain the level of environmental detail and activity they want throughout Leondia. Rather than offering separate graphics and performance options, Rockstar has built the console experience around a single presentation target, which makes sense considering the numerous of different configurations available even on just consoles.

The PS5 Pro's additional horsepower doesn't change the core limitation. While its upgraded GPU allows Rockstar to improve visual clarity details that aren't available on the standard PS5, its CPU is only modestly improved. This matters more than you may think, because running a game at 60fps requires the system to complete its work for each frame in roughly half the time available at 30fps.

This also means Xbox Series X|S owners shouldn't expect a different outcome. Rockstar's 30fps target applies across Microsoft's current console lineup, and neither the Series X nor the less powerful Series S has been positioned to offer a higher frame-rate option. There is no indication that a future patch will introduce one, either.

For players who prioritize smoother performance, the news will undoubtedly be disappointing, particularly given how much time has passed since the current console generation began. 30 FPS, especially after playing at a higher framerate, can be difficult to go back to. However, Rockstar appears committed to preserving the visual detail and complexity it has built into Grand Theft Auto 6 rather than compromising that experience to pursue a higher frame rate. Console players should therefore approach the November 19 release expecting 30fps, not a performance mode that might arrive soon after, or even later at all.

articles.title: VisionQuest’s Blink-And-You-Miss-It Scarlet Witch Detail Fixes a Major Fan Complaint
articles.summary: There were many thrilling moments and exciting updates in VisionQuest, but arguably the two biggest were the appearance of Billy Maximoff (and his reunion with Tommy and Vision) and the post-credits scene confirming that Wanda Maximoff is alive. Although Wanda has yet to reunite with her sons or Vision, and it's unclear when or if […]
articles.content:
For one, the post-credits scene confirmed that Doctor Doom himself has come to collect Wanda, saying he will take the Scarlet Witch's power for himself, suggesting that Wanda may actually be a villain under Doom's control in Avengers: Doomsday . Additionally, though, Agatha All Along confirmed that Billy, who doesn't have most of his memories from the Hex beyond the existence of his brother, doesn't accept Wanda as his mom. In part, this is because he was raised by the Kaplans for about three years, and he therefore sees them as his parents, but it also revealed some seeming animosity for Wanda. That certainly rubbed fans the wrong way, but now, a blink-and-you-miss-it detail has suggested this major fan complaint may be a thing of the past.

When Billy appeared in VisionQuest , most of the attention was on this reunion, how emotional it was to see Tommy and Billy finally back together, and the moment in which Vision pulls Billy in for a hug. It was therefore very easy to miss the minor details on Billy's jacket, but eagle-eyed fans have now discovered that this jacket includes none other than the Scarlet Witch's crown. Already, that connection was there in light of the crown that appeared on Billy's head in Agatha All Along , but the fact that Billy drew this symbol onto his jacket himself means that he almost certainly has come around when it comes to how he feels about Wanda, and that's great news.

Wiccan has added Scarlet Witch’s crown to his jacket in ‘VISIONQUEST’ (via sarahyoung_costumedesign | IG) pic.twitter.com/m9XhoBR230

Hopefully, this easy-to-miss detail means that, once the family is finally reunited, Billy will be much more open to accepting Wanda as his mom. Already, audiences have seen signs of that change in Billy's overall feelings about the Maximoffs, given that he at first calls Vision “sir” and then is pulled into a hug. VisionQuest also concludes with Tommy and Vision headed to have dinner with Billy (and presumably Agatha as well ) in New Jersey. Yet, things are guaranteed to be more complicated with Wanda, especially given her current status with Doctor Doom, which means that, sadly, this fan-favorite MCU family is still far from a happy ending, if one is ever coming.

How do you think the Maximoffs will be reunited, and do you think it will happen in Doomsday ? Let us know in the comments down below.

articles.title: Brad Pitt Wants To Make a Sequel to The 2025 Hit That Set His Own Box Office Record
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Apple Brad Pitt is currently out promoting The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, the highly anticipated sequel centering on his character from Once Upon a Time in Hollywood. Pitt won an Academy Award for portraying Cliff Booth, so it's exciting to see him take on the role again but it is not the only sequel he's […]
articles.content:
In the sports drama from director Joseph Kosinski, Pitt plays Sonny Hayes, a racer-for-hire who joins a struggling Formula One team in the hopes of turning it around. The movie became a monster hit , grossing over $600 million. That made it the highest-grossing film from Apple and of Pitt's legendary career. Given that level of success, it makes sense that Pitt would want to return to the role of Hayes and while promoting The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , the actor discussed that filming for the long-awaited Ocean's 14 is set to start late next year, but he also gave an update on the future of F1 .

While being interviewed by Variety , Brad Pitt talked about Ocean's 14 before being asked if there was another movie he was interested in returning to. Without much hesitation, Pitt responded, “Yeah, yeah, actually. F1 .” The interviewer noted that the film is going to happen, as it was announced soon after the box office success of F1 was official that a sequel was being discussed. Apple had critical darlings like The Killers of the Flower Moon , but they hadn't released a major commercial hit to that point, so F1 was a welcome change.

Along with plans for a sequel, there was also talk of Apple turning F1 into an entire franchise. They could release several future film installments, maybe a TV show on their impressive streaming service (likely focusing on other racers rather than Hayes in that case), or even possibly branch out into the world of video games. In early 2026, the F1 sequel was officially greenlit. Apple understands that it has a legitimate hit with F1 , as fans of the sport, fans of sports films in general, and fans of Pitt will flock to see it.

Producer and F1 champion Lewis Hamilton mentioned how they wanted to take the time to ensure any further entries are as accurate as the original, so it might take a while to get one. As noted, F1 made history for Brad Pitt by becoming the highest-grossing film of his career. Looking at Hollywood's track record, sequels tend to perform better than the first installment; a follow-up to F1 would likely break that record. There's also a good chance that Ocean's 14 is a hit that grosses nearly as much, so Pitt has a lot to be excited about. If the F1 sequel is anywhere near as good as the first, Apple and Pitt have a special franchise on their hands.

What do you want to see from an F1 sequel? Let us know in the comments!

articles.title: Steven Spielberg Calls ‘The Odyssey’ a ‘Showstopper’ and ‘One of the Greatest Things’ Matt Damon Has Ever Done
articles.summary: After a weeklong run of screening Christopher Nolan's “The Odyssey,” Universal saved the best for last, bringing out Steven Spielberg to moderate a one-on-one Q&A. As the film ended and the house lights went up, the pair walked out to a standing ovation from an audience of about 600 guild members and voters who had […]
articles.content:
After a weeklong run of screening Christopher Nolan ‘s " The Odyssey ," Universal saved the best for last, bringing out Steven Spielberg to moderate a one-on-one Q&A.

As the film ended and the house lights went up, the pair walked out to a standing ovation from an audience of about 600 guild members and voters who had come out to see the film — many on repeat viewings.

Before Spielberg had a moment to praise Nolan for the $1.8 billion blockbuster, it was Nolan who stepped in and humbly told Spielberg, "I just have to take a minute, because I've known you a long time, but I've never done a Q&A with you. When I was a younger man and a dear boy watching your movies, I don't think I ever really envisioned this moment where you would be asking questions about my film." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Patrick Stewart's Final Movie Is 'Avengers: Doomsday'; He Said Before His Death That 'I Can’t Imagine Retiring. I’ll Forever Be an Actor' Florence Pugh Fires Back at Video Claiming She Used Plastic Surgery to Change Her Face: 'Disturbing' How 'People Can't Tell the Difference Between Aging and Surgery'

Spielberg told Nolan he had seen the film in Imax and called it "a showstopper."

When asked why now, and why he had chosen to adapt Homer's poem, Nolan answered, "I always find it hard to figure out what to do next. Probably one of the reasons, if it's been unpredictable, as you say, it's because it's always a surprise to me as well. I do one project at a time. I'm not very good at developing multiple things at the same time, so I finish one film and then I look for what might be next."

He continued, "What hadn't really been done in the modern era was Greek mythology and I think the reason is because it hadn't been done definitively. Part of the reason was because of the mythological elements; the visual effects techniques weren't really available in the 1930s or the 1950s. When the great eras of the classical world, the world of antiquity, was big in Hollywood. ‘The Odyssey' hadn't been done on this scale with this movie budget, with the resources of modern technology: shooting on Imax, using visual effects and all the rest." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Nolan also talked about building his cast and choosing Matt Damon to play Odysseus. "This is one of the greatest things Matt has ever done as an actor," Spielberg said.

Nolan said, "Matt occurred to me right away because I've done two films with him in small parts. So I know from my own experience on the floor how incredible he is as an actor and how great he is to work with. How he's just an incredible team member. He's an incredible creative force. He's not just thinking about his own part. He's thinking about the whole narrative, which is a great asset. But also, he's grown up on camera. You know, from that kid in ‘Saving Private Ryan.' He has this ability to open up a story and take us on a journey, in empathetic terms; that's incredibly powerful."

Spielberg took a moment to tell Nolan that one of his favorite scenes in the film featured Samantha Morton as the witchy goddess Circe, and he wanted to know how Nolan pulled it off. Spielberg said, "She was wonderful … That's one of my favorite scenes in the whole movie, where they all turn into pigs."

Nolan explained he didn't want to shoot in front of a green screen or use tracking markers. "I wanted to be able to define the process." He said he watched transformation movies such as "An American Werewolf in London" and even Neil Jordan's "A Company of Wolves" for inspiration.

He revealed it was a collaboration with both the visual effects and special effects departments as they navigated the challenge. "They came up with these heads that have a skull underneath that's fractured, but it's held together with magnets and then it's covered in a particular type of silicone skin that looked exactly wonderfully real, but was very flexible. So we built these heads of the guys, and each take, she could go around the table and do whatever she wanted and manipulate these guys however she wanted in the most horrible ways."

"The Odyssey" opened in July to a $264.1 million global debut, the biggest of Nolan's career. It has since crossed $1.8 billion, becoming his highest-grossing film. Universal and Nolan's team are continuing to focus on the format. Nearly every Los Angeles screening is tagged Imax 70mm, 70mm or 35mm, reminding viewers that the film was shot entirely using Imax cameras and built to be judged on a screen the size of a building and not on a laptop or their home TV using the Academy digital portal.

articles.title: The '90s Weirdest Spider-Man Story Gets Even Stranger for New Marvel TV Show, According to Report
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Spider-Man's Clone Saga will be the backbone of a new Marvel TV show for Prime Video, and this bizarre '90s comic book plot is about to get even weirder. When Spider-Noir premiered earlier this year and even earned Primetime Emmy recognition, it seemed like the streamer had a new franchise on their hands, which made […]
articles.content:
One of those projects that seemed the closest to actually happening is a series that riffs on Spider-Man's Clone Saga, and now new details reveal how different it really will be. These details hail from Apocalyptic Horseman , a social media personality known for reporting scoops on upcoming projects. According to them, the film will follow Kaine and Ben Reilly, the same names as the Spider-Man clones from Marvel comics, only this time they'll be brothers on opposite sides of the law. Ben will be a cop, Kaine a criminal, and their relationship becomes more symbiotic after they gain spider-like superpowers that only work around each other.

The report goes on to reveal two additional details for the series, the first being that Miles Warren will be the main antagonist and that both Ben and Kaine will have to team up to solve a murder. That first reveal shouldn't surprise anyone who reads comics regularly, since Warren is the legal name of the Spider-Man antagonist The Jackal who is responsible for all those clones, but the second is interesting. Fresh off the heels of Lanterns taking the superhero genre in the direction of True Detective , it's easy to see how a pitch like this came together for Prime Video, especially after that DC series was a hit.

All the changes being made to the larger “Clone Saga” storyline are pretty bizarre anyway, and that's on top of the comic book plot being weird on its own. In the pages of Marvel comics, the '90s Clone Saga (technically the second with that name) has multiple Spider-Men operating at one time and at one point tried to pull the twist that Ben Reilly was the original person and Peter Parker was actually a clone of him. It all culminated in the reveal that Norman Osborn was alive and manipulating heroes and villains alike in his quest to torment Peter.

What these details about the show confirm, though, is that the same problems with Spider-Man spinoffs are going to persist well into the future. Even though details about the show confirm that elements of the comics are being used to bring it to life, the series will seemingly be totally separate from any larger Spider-Man mythology and may not even use the name “Spider-Man” in the slightest. Naturally the infinite reach of the “Spider-Verse” makes this feasible, but it has proven to be a problem before with the many Sony-made spinoff movies, and even Spider-Noir to an extent. Will Marvel fans flock to seeing a version of this beloved (but contrived) story on TV or is it doomed before it even gets started?

articles.title: The Batman's Robert Pattinson Is the New 007, So Now Is the Perfect Time to Discover James Bond's Wild Comic Book History
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Dymanite Entertainment We finally have a new James Bond and it's Edward. Oh, wait, wrong decade. Robert Pattinson, who is also playing Batman in The Batman series of movies, has been cast as the British spy. Pattinson has spent the years since his role in Twilight showing that he was more than a heart throb, taking a […]
articles.content:
James Bond was created by Ian Fleming, a character meant to play in the high stakes world of Cold War spies, and the character first appeared in the novel Casino Royale . Fleming ended up writing numerous Bond stories, they became movies, and that opened the floodgates. Licensed comics have been big business for years and Bond's history with comics goes back further than you think. With writer Grant Morrison about to write Bond comics and Pattinson's casting, it's a perfect time to ask M for the files on 007's missions in the world of the funny pages.

The first James Bond movie was Dr. No in 1962 and right away, James made his way to the comics. The movie was adapted in the United Kingdom in Classic Illustrated #158A, telling the film on the page. It would get reprinted in Europe by Dell Publishing in 1962, and then in the United States by DC Comics in 1963's Showcase #43. While the Bond movies were popular, the Dr. No adaptation didn't make as much of a splash and Bond comics were a thing of the past.

18 years later, Marvel Comics would try their hands at it with an adaptation of 1981's For Your Eyes Only . This one was popular, resulting in it being reprinted in a single magazine format and a collected edition. 1983 would see the House of Ideas publish an adaptation of Octopussy in magazine format, but it wasn't as big. However, there would be another long drought of Bond comics until 1989, when getting James Bond comics on a more regular basis became normal for a few years. The comic industry was in the midst of a boom, with numerous licensed comics popping up all over.

It started with an adaptation of License to Kill from Eclipse Comics, which was illustrated by Mike Grell, who was getting a lot of praise for his work on Green Arrow: The Longbow Hunters , and would lead to a both hardcover and paperback collected editions. Grell would have the distinction of being the first comic creator to write an original James Bond story, Permission to Die, which would be published over the course of two years from Eclipse.

GoldenEye was the big mid '90s Bond reboot and Topps Comics, the trading card company trying their hand at comics, would get the license to produce Bond stories. However, the second issue was delayed due to problems with its cover art, leading Topps to can the whole adaptation and scrap their plans for the license, which had included an all-new ongoing. However, the spy would have to wait no time at all for comics to come calling again. The mid '90s were also the time when Dark Horse Comics was putting out the best licensed comics around and they had their own deal.

See, the license to use a character and the license to adapt a movie can be separate. So, when other companies were making the adaptations, Dark Horse got the license to produce its own Bond stories in 1992. The company produced a number of Bond minis – Serpent's Tooth, Silent Armageddon, Light of My Death, Shattered Helix, Minute of Midnight , and The Quasimodo Gambit – between '92 and 1995. However, Bond comics never really seemed to catch on, leading Dark Horse to give up the license.

Bond comics would disappear for a while, with even the Casino Royale reboot not being adapted. The 2000s would go by with nary a Bond book to found. The '10s would dawn and still no Bond until 2014, when Dynamite Entertainment, who had been making a name for themselves with licensed comics (you might know them better as the publisher of The Boys ) acquired it. They decided to go in a different direction than others, by publishing stories set in two different timelines, focusing more on the literary version of the spy.

The first was set before his adventures in book Casino Royale and the second was more comtemporary, telling the stories of his adventures in the present day. It was an interesting way to approach the character, allowing creators to go a variety of directions with him. The first book, titled James Bond , premiered in 2015, and James Bond Origins would drop in 2018, with various miniseries and spin-offs getting published. The main series boasted talent like Warren Ellis, Kieron Gillen, Benjamin Percy, Andy Diggle, Jody Houser, Declan Shalvey, Garth Ennis, and more. The upcoming Grant Morrison reboot is just the latest in a long line of Bond comics.

The history of James Bond in the comic industry is an interesting one. There are few characters created outside comics who are better for comics than him, but it never really happened. One gets the impression that the Bond license is one that is tightly controlled by the owners, which made it hard to do anything but adaptations for a while. Bond is one of those characters who has become an indelible part of pop culture but honestly, it feels like the only times anyone has been serious about making comics starring the spy work was when Dark Horse had the license and then Dynamite.

Bond can be a tough sell in the 21st century. He's a character from a very specific time in history and he was tailor-made for it. It'll be interesting to see how Amazon handles the character; the Daniel Craig version went gritty, so maybe this time we'll get a more polished take. However, one of the best things about comics is the fact that you don't have to try to change the character to make him appeal to an audience that isn't into him. While the history of James Bond comics is one of starts and stops, I feel like we've finally reached the perfect era of comics for the character.

articles.title: Ted: The Animated Series Confirms Return of Peacock Series' Best Characters With One Glaring Absence
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of UGT / Fuzzy Door / MRC Ted is coming back to Peacock with a new animated series hitting later this December, and the first look at the new show has confirmed that two of the best characters from the live-action TV series are coming back. But there's still one major absence that fans have immediately noticed. Ted: The Animated Series is […]
articles.content:
But with the success of the Ted TV series with Peacock, fans had gotten attached to those earlier depictions of the franchise's characters . This is especially true for the members of the Bennett family, and thankfully it's been confirmed that Matty and Susan are set to return to the new animated series with Scott Grimes and Alanna Ubach likely reprising their roles. You can check out the first look at them below, but Giorgia Whigham's Blaire unfortunately seems unaccounted for right now.

Ted: The Animated Series is set back in the canon of the Ted films, and that means Mark Wahlberg returns as the older version of John for the occasion. The Ted TV series technically was in line with the films, but had taken on a whole life of its own with fans online especially with the different iterations of Matty and Susan Bennett. The TV series had fully invented new versions of John's parents (who had been portrayed by Ralph Garman and Alex Bortstein in the first Ted film, and even had different names), so it's a great sign to see them folded into the animated series.

But their return also raises a few questions. It's likely that Ted: The Animated Series isn't too concerned with having a tight timeline of events, but Matty and Susan should technically be in the eighties by this point given that they were already a bit older in the 1990s. And through the first trailer, Blaire doesn't seem to appear either. She was the standout brand new addition to the formula in the TV series, so there's a hope that she makes a surprise appearance as an older version of herself in one of these animated series episodes to come.

Ted: The Animated Series will be making its debut with Peacock on Thursday, December 17th with eight episodes all available at once. Additional episodes of the animated series planned for a release sometime in 2027, but no concrete release date has been announced as of this time. The core cast of the films are returning to reprise their respective roles with Seth MacFarlane as Ted, Mark Wahlberg as John, Amanda Seyfried as Sam, and Jessica Barth as Tami-Lynn all set alongside new additions Kyle Mooney as Apollo and Liz Richman as Ruth.

With the Ted franchise continuing its story through the animated series, it unfortunately means that the live-action TV series is likely not going to return anytime soon. Seth MacFarlane noted that while the production team and Peacock had deemed the series a success, it was just “too expensive” to keep producing . articles.title: The Internet Can’t Stop Talking About People’s Mouths In Netflix’s The Christmas Switch. I Can’t Unsee It
articles.summary: If you haven't watched this yet, give it two minutes. You can't unsee it.
articles.content:
I’m pretty good about keeping an eye on the Christmas movies schedule , but I was a few days late to Netflix’s The Christmas Switch . (Can you blame a girl when Hallmark is over here dropping holiday time loop bangers ?) The new romantic holiday comedy was written and filmed in Sweden, but you’d seemingly never know it from the English version, which is dubbed over in English, and has the actors’ mouths matching the English words, as well. Let's talk about this strange magic.

It was uncanny. It made the viewing experience weird. I didn’t particularly like it. And it turned a perfectly OK holiday film into something far stranger.

The Christmas Switch was made available for anyone with a Netflix subscription on November 12th, so it's been around for a few days. It’s currently in the Top 10 in the US, along with fellow Christmas flicks The Gospel of Christmas and A Dog’s Perfect Christmas . So, it’s safe to say a lot of people have witnessed this mouth edit phenomenon.

Listen, we all know dubbing is annoying in general. I’ve watched every season of the now-canceled Maxton Hall on Amazon Prime Video, and I don’t like the mouths not matching the English language version, either. Still, at least that feels authentic. And there’s always the option to watch just with subtitles. (This is true for The Christmas Switch too; it’s just not the option that comes up on English-language Netflix first.)

articles.content:
EXCLUSIVE : When Gladys Knight sang “Midnight Train to Georgia” on the season six finale of American Idol , backed by Ben Stiller, Jack Black and Robert Downey Jr., nobody thought that twenty years later the team behind the show would be taking her lyrics so literally.

LA proved too much for the show, it seems, as the ABC music competition takes its live shows to the suburbs of Atlanta for the first time in its 25-year history.

Deadline revealed in September that the Ryan Seacrest-hosted show would be relocating, but it is only one of a number of changes to the show as it heads into Season 25 (or Season 10 on ABC). blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The other major change to Idol is that there is a surprising new path to America's Vote as the show eschews Hollywood Week for the first time. Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

Contestants will no longer be heading to Hollywood (or Nashville, as it was last season), but instead judges Luke Bryan, Lionel Richie and Carrie Underwood will award 25 Golden Tickets, sending hopefuls straight to Hawaii.

"This is a major departure, major changes coming," American Idol showrunner Megan Michaels Wolflick told Deadline ahead of its return on Monday, February 8, 2027.

By cutting out Hollywood Week, American Idol can get to the live shows quicker. The show will kick off with three audition episodes, followed by two shows in Hawaii before going live. "The auditions and the live shows are the bread and butter for this show and the process of a Hollywood Week is really a culling process that we were televising," Michaels Wolflick added. "Going to America's Vote is what this show is about. Hollywood was a metaphor."

The move essentially allows viewers to vote on their favorites earlier. It coincides with the 25th anniversary, hopefully giving it a Survivor 50 -style celebration.

Michaels Wolflick is known for regularly freshening up the format over the years, for instance, becoming the first major competition show to introduce social voting last season. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"It keeps people on their toes," she said. "We're still keeping the cornerstones of the house, but we are just remodeling a room. The promise is still there but it's really nice to switch it up and we're keeping the integrity and the dream of the show."

The top 25 from the auditions will be sent straight to the Disney resort Aulani in Ko Olina, Hawaii to perform. They will also be joined by one more singer, who can score America's Golden Ticket.

Three hopefuls who did not receive one of the tickets from the judges will be featured during the Country Music Awards and on social media with fans voting on social media – Facebook, Instagram and TikTok – as to who will get the spot. Votes will be cast between November 18 and 25 with the winner being announced on ABC's Dick Clark's New Year's Rockin' Eve.

Michaels Wolflick said that last season's social voting went well and she was excited to do it again. She noted that people on different platforms voted differently; unsurprisingly, Facebook voters were older. "The win for me was the growth across the season and I still feel there's so much more ground to cover next year," she added.

American Idol has filmed its live shows in Los Angeles for the last 24 years but will spend eight weeks at Trillith Live, outside of Atlanta.

"We've always been kind of looking at it because there's been other shows that have moved over the past couple of years," she said. "The thing about Idol is we have always traveled. We have filmed [auditions] in Georgia for many years. It didn't feel that disruptive for us."

The move is bad news for Los Angeles, which saw 40% fewer unscripted TV shoot days in the second quarter of 2026 compared to the same period last year. Idol is following shows such as The Masked Singer , which moved to New Jersey, with other big competition shows such as The Voice and America's Got Talent eyeing moves out of California as well.

California's tax credit does include large-scale competition shows but Deadline understands Idol wasn't eligible, which means the move to Georgia, which offers up to a 30% tax credit for unscripted and reality television productions that spend at least $500,000 in the state, makes more financial sense.

"Georgia wants to incentivize filming. Our state [California] does not," she said. "We barely ever got outside the studio. We weren't outside at the Hollywood Bowl. The dream of the show is to perform on an incredible stage with an incredible band with hair and makeup and wardrobe at the top tier level in the industry, and we can still provide that."

Soon after American Idol premiered on Fox in 2002, it started to see competition. There was USA Network's Nashville Star , NBC's Fame and CBS' Rock Star.

But in 2011, Fox and NBC took bigger swings to compete with the Fremantle and 19 Entertainment-produced show including U.S. versions of The X Factor and The Voice.

The X Factor may well be back as a new iteration is in development at Fox . ABC also has new music competition series Who's In The Band? launching in the summer, after Idol finishes its run.

Michaels Wolflick said that as long as these shows aren't going head-to-head, like they did back in the day, there's room for more music on television. "It used to be more Hunger Games ," she added. "I still have the Hunger Games mentality when making [ Idol ] in my own head. I really do. I'm always [thinking], ‘How can we change? How can we adapt? What can we do?' I'm very competitive."

articles.title: Hudson Williams and His Hairstylist Aika Flores Really Are That Close
articles.summary: The 'Heated Rivalry' breakout has had a whirlwind year, and his groomer has been along for the ride the entire time: "We're like family now."

It was early December 2025 when actor Hudson Williams met celebrity groomer Aika Flores . His queer Canadian hockey series, Heated Rivalry , had been out for just over a week, but the show was already catching fire on social media and at workplace water coolers. The pair met when Flores was hired by her close friend to do grooming for a cover shoot with Timid Magazine .

"[My friend and editor-in-chief] Henry was telling me, ‘It's this show that's on the second episode. I think it's going to get big. People are already talking about it. He's hot,'" Flores tells The Hollywood Reporter about the pitch on Williams. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories THR Cover Story Alix Earle Bares All: How the TikToker Is Becoming Beauty's Next Billion-Dollar Mogul General News 'Heated Rivalry' Star Connor Storrie, 'Obsession' Ingenue Inde Navarette and 'Backrooms' Filmmaker Kane Parsons Set as BAFTA U.S. Breakouts

Flash forward 11 months, and she and Williams are sprawled out on a couch in the green room of THR's New York photo studio. It's a rare break in filming for Williams, who's knee deep in filming the second season of Heated Rivalry . As predicted, the show blew up, became a cultural phenomenon and launched the 25-year-old Canadian actor into an overnight sensation and a certified heartthrob. It didn't take long for Williams' authentic appreciation for skincare to land him a brand ambassadorship with his favorite Korean skincare company Skin 1004.

But Williams has had virtually no time over the last year between returning to the hockey romance series, his latest show AMC+'s Yaga and a slew of other roles he's booked in the wake of his breakout. It's been intense. And Flores has been by his side the entire time.

"The vibes were so good," says Williams of their first meeting. "I was so tired that day, but we were already getting into our early lives, where we grew up." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

That one-day booking for a U.S. press day turned into jetsetting around the world together this past year for media appearances and red carpets. "[His team] wanted to see first if we got along, and then they booked [me for the rest of the tour] while we were doing the shoot," Flores says.

"She was grounding, chill, funny," says Williams. "Sometimes over-talkative people are just a little bit much in the morning, especially when [there are] always late nights. Those people that always have energy. I'm like, whoa, whoa, whoa."

Flores reminds Williams that he's pretty high energy — except when he's in her chair getting ready. "Quiet time," he says.

This is in high contrast to only minutes earlier, when the pair were joking around shooting video content: Williams taking a stab at being the one to pamper Flores for a change, Flores attempting to get the actor ready as he jumped out of the chair and dodge her hands. The horseplay on set might have one assume that they are close friends. "We're like family now," Flores says. Williams describes how he's become "Uncle Hudson" to Flores' son. "He made me brush his teeth," he says, fondly.

Uncle Hudson has been known to prep for bedtime stories with the same dedication he applies to scenes, using voices for the characters, something Flores jokes that she and her wife don't even do. "I was sort of nervous, I had to play Santa," Williams says. "I was like, ‘I hope he's not judging me.'" blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

That almost familial closeness helped Williams through a whirlwind year. After Heated Rivalry finished airing around Christmas 2025, his schedule exploded with late-night tapings, Golden Globes presenting, Olympic torch-bearing, Milan runway walking and more life-changing experiences. Through it all, Flores, along with his CAA branding agent Leilani Houston and stylist Anastasia Walker, have been by his side. "It's been great because honestly. We call our group chats the quad squad," Williams says.

"Yesterday we hung out until 3 a.m., after a day where we were up in the morning, and it was a 12-hour shooting day because we just love each other so much," Williams adds. "We all take care of each other. It's kind of like a maternal energy towards everyone. It feels like we're sisters braiding each other's hair or something — with alcohol."

Williams leans on the quad when online commentary gets intense. "A lot of times social media is just inherently mean, and so everyone gets shot at online," he continues. “We always have each other, and there's a feeling that since we're always aligned and we always have this group that we will always be together." Flores says they often laugh the hate off because it's the only way to go about it. "It's outrageous, so it's so funny," Williams says. "It's like speculation or they make it up," adds Flores.

"When we come across it, we're like, ‘Oh my God, did you know that I got shot yesterday? Did you know that I'm actually really problematic, I guess?' We just laugh because it's so stupid," she continues. "That's what's nice, is having each other," adds Williams. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Even as Williams signature heartthrob hair has been a hit online, plenty of people have speculated that Flores is somehow forcing Williams into looks he doesn't want. "I want my hair to be the same," the actor clarifies. "It's how he likes it, and I just elevate it, and then we bounce off ideas," Flores adds.

The pair also like to take risks, his daring Met Gala look of exaggerated cat eyes and sculpted wet hair landing on many best-of lists. "She popped off with the Met," says Williams. "We like to have fun, and not take anything too serious. [We] just try things, be bold."

Heated Rivalry is taking up much of his time lately, rejoining his co-star Connor Storrie to film the show's highly anticipated next season in Toronto. "It's going good, but it's sad," Williams says, referencing the material they'll be tackling in the next season. It's based on author Rachel Reid's follow-up The Long Game , which show creator Jacob Tierney has previously referred to as "Sex Scenes From A Marriage ."

There's not much Williams can say about what they're getting up to on the set, but he did note that the return made him a little nervous. "Even the joining cast, they immediately picked up on the vibe and were so sweet. We're all supportive of each other. It's just a really fun time. Still feels tiny, [it's] just crazy," adds Williams. "It's just a bigger family now."

For The Hollywood Reporter ‘s 10th Beauty Issue, Williams and Flores talked about “evil” hair, that time he got scolded by a security guard (and the internet) for lighting a smoke on the streets of Milan, and why in times of exhaustion, Williams likes to “take a nap on Aika.”

FLORES I think my favorite look has to be the Met [Gala].

WILLIAMS She popped off with the Met.

FLORES It was so collaborative between me and [stylist] Anastasia that for, I feel like months, we were planning it. As soon as [Hudson] got invited, we were [planning]. We knew from the beginning we weren't going to do a black suit. That's just not his personality, [or any] of our personalities.

WILLIAMS I wasn't even trying to smoke that in the street, but I was like, “Will I have time to smoke it there?” I think it was Lei Lei, who was like, “I don't think you have time.” So I asked, “Should I just smoke it while I'm walking?” But I felt like with the suit, how we worked with Armani to make that. articles.title: New PS5 Console Update Has to Be Downloaded to Play GTA 6
articles.summary: With Grand Theft Auto 6 finally arriving on November 19, fans don't have long to wait before they can jump into Leonida, but PlayStation 5 players have one more thing to check off their list first. Sony has issued a new PS5 system software update that players must download before they can play GTA 6. […]
articles.content:
The last thing any player wants is to have to download a system update when trying to boot up GTA 6 for the first time . This is especially true for those who have preloaded the game or taken time off from work to play it. However, having the game installed doesn't necessarily mean the system update has been downloaded and it is best to verify this ahead of time. Be sure to check your console's system software now to see if you need to update.

The latest PS5 firmware update is available now and it is required before being able to play Grand Theft Auto 6 . The update is approximately 1.2GB, making it relatively small and should go through quickly. Still, any delay on November 19th means less time playing GTA 6 . According to Sony's patch notes, the update introduces security fixes to the PS5 system software. However, the company hasn't explained why this particular update is mandatory for GTA 6 .

This is the third PS5 firmware update released within a month making the matter more curiosity. The updates did occur around times there were reports of hackers attempting to bypass the PS5's security protections. This could be for increased security, especially around such a large release, but Sony have not confirmed this.

Sony Interactive has issued a PS5 system software update that is required before playing Grand Theft Auto VI. Players should download this update prior to midnight on November 19 so that they’re ready to play on launch day, November 19.

Fortunately, installing the update is straightforward. The update is found in the Settings menu, particularly in the System tab. From there, simply open the System Software tab and verify there are no available updates or go ahead and update your console via the System Software Update and Settings button. If you have automatic system updates enabled, the update may already be installed. Still, it is highly recommended to check just to be safe.

It's worth emphasizing that this is a PS5 system update, not a separate Grand Theft Auto 6 patch. Players who have already downloaded the game will still need the latest firmware before launching it. With the game launching tomorrow, there is only a single day to update your console to prepare for GTA 6 .

I'm not saying the palace's social media team needs to write Bond 26 , but I wouldn't mind seeing what they'd do with a martini joke.

I love that they chose that particular passage from Moonraker . Think about how many actors have stepped into Bond's shoes since Sean Connery first wore the tuxedo. Everybody recognizes the silhouette, but the person inside it has changed quite a bit over six decades. The statement continued:

That's a lovely endorsement, especially since casting a new Bond tends to spark strong opinions. Fan reactions to Pattinson's casting have been pretty mixed, and I'm sure there will be plenty more debate once a trailer for his first 007 flick arrives. I appreciate that Fleming's estate welcomed him by reminding everyone why the character has survived so many reinventions.

articles.title: 5 1980s Cartoon Theme Songs That All ’80s Kids Remember More Than the Actual Shows
articles.summary: Back in the day, when the theme songs for TV shows were still a thing unto themselves, you didn't need to know anything about a series in order to enjoy its intro music. A single, brief tune would drive you stumbling towards the TV set in anticipation, without you even knowing what was going on. […]
articles.content:
And here's the funny thing. For all that, you would likely find a lot of kids who grew up during that decade who could name some of these TV shows today. Many of them might not have watched the cartoons in their entirety or only stuck around long enough to hear the music. But if you play the opening themes, they can quickly be heard singing along with every word. That's what a great TV theme does. It remains long after you've long forgotten the shows themselves.

If you were a child of the '80s, you probably remember The Real Ghostbusters theme song within moments of hearing it. The animated series debuted following the runaway success of the 1984 film and faced some stiff competition. Luckily, the opening theme captured the spirit of everything wonderful about the franchise. It was fast-paced, infectious, and just spooky enough to motivate you to leap out of bed on a Saturday morning.

Ray Parker Jr.'s version of the movie theme didn't need much help in terms of popularity—it was already fantastic. But the cartoon's producers decided to take the musical theme elsewhere, when it introduced the team with a spotlight on the chaos of the supernatural city they dealt with each week. The cartoon's theme song was actually a new version of the movie's song but with a more uplifting rock vibe. And although musician/singer Starz Vanderlocket is cited as the singer, there are debates about the true vocalist of the song. Regardless, it's an awesome song that is iconic, memorable, and oh-so-fun to sing aloud.

There's just something so wonderfully preposterous about Inspector Gadget . He was meant to be an ace detective, but he's forever bumbling into trouble while Penny and Brain, his granddaughter and her dog, are getting all the work done behind the scenes, and somehow that's even better. But if there's one thing that everyone remembers it's that playfully catchy theme tune.

The first track is a catchy, immediately recognizable song that has the distinctive right feel for this cartoon, like spy music – not quite serious, but definitely adventurous. That's perfect for a cartoon about a very quirky detective with an infinite number of strange mechanical contraptions. The music can set the tone of the show for you even before Gadget begins trying to do himself in, and you can almost hear the excitement of those Saturday mornings when you just think about it, even if many people can still hum it long after he forgot exactly what scheme Dr. Claw had cooked up that week.

Some cartoon themes were catchy. Some played you into thinking you were about to go into an epic fight to save the world from evil. ThunderCats was undoubtedly in the latter camp. There was a huge film scale to the theme music for ThunderCats that gave the series an instant feeling of grandeur. It grabbed you before Lion-O even strutted onto the screen.

The song that played in the very beginning was a piece of music that was designed to fit the fantasy nature of the show. It had thumping drums, sweeping music, and enough heroic energy that almost any kid watching would have wanted to have their own Sword of Omens. It was a fantastic, slightly over-the-top opening for the show about a bunch of cats who were trying to make a home on an alien world. The animation of the opening segment helped a lot, but the music itself did a lot of work, and I still find the opening music makes me think of sitting in front of the TV and waiting for Lion-O to give his battle cry. It's one of the few songs that can truly get me hyped and wishing I was a fantasy warrior.

Now this is my all-time favorite without a doubt. Cowabunga! Plenty of classic 1980s cartoon theme songs to choose from, but not much beats the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles ‘ original opening. As soon as the theme kicks in, you know what to expect. Four pizza-obsessed turtles are about to burst through the sewer, and someone is inevitably going to reference a pizza delivery while they're at it.

The theme does something very clever by giving you all four characters, one after the other: Leonardo was the leader, Donatello did machines, Raphael was cool but rude and Michelangelo was a party dude. You can't help but sing along to those lines. The theme song also brings a bit of joy to the series that fits the vibrant animation style – the original TV series was a runaway success and the song is probably just as well known. Even people who haven't watched an episode of the series in years are probably still able to get all the way through most of the lyrics – impressive for a theme about mutant turtles.

The original DuckTales theme is easily one of the most catchy TV tunes of the whole decade. You might not remember every single challenge that Scrooge McDuck faced, but there's a good chance you can still bust out the opening lines without a single hiccup. That's the sort of durability most TV programs would kill for. The only reason this song tops TMNT in my opinion, is that its Disney appeal might have opened it up to a slightly wider audience and demographic than the Turtles. Heck, I think I even had childhood friends and neighbors who could sing this song and dance to it without being major fans of the cartoon.

Written by Mark Mueller and sung by Jeff Pescetto, the song is almost perfectly crafted. It's lively and a little daring, with enough hooks to stay with you all day. The lyrics summed up everything that made the show great, too, with mysteries to uncover, treasure to be had, and the McDuck family constantly getting into trouble. In fact, that Disney thought the theme song was so great that they revived the show in 2017. That's the kind of legacy that translates to lots of great cartoons in the 1980s – DuckTales had something that just can't be overcome.

Which of these classic '80s cartoon theme songs still lives rent-free in your head? Did we leave out one of your all-time favorites? Share your memories and let us know which opening theme you could still sing word for word in the comments below!

Taku Kishimoto returns from the first season to handle the scripts, Yo Moriyama returns to provide the character designs, and Yuki Hayashi returns to compose the music. But as demonstrated with this new trailer, the action seems to have been better established this time around compared to when the anime first began.

The second half of Sakamoto Days' debut season had been received much better than the first, and this second season is teasing it will all going in that same great direction. articles.title: Cult '90s Horror Movie Officially Getting a Sequel 31 Years Later, And the Title Is Perfect
articles.summary: IMAGE COURTESY OF A-PIX ENTERTAINMENT 1995's Ice Cream Man didn't entirely set the box office on fire when it was released initially; more viewers probably saw the Rifftrax version than the original release. Yet it's become a cult hit that refuses to die, with Clint Howard as a frozen treat maker who uses some particularly gross ingredients in his confections, […]
articles.content:
Howard has been trying to get a sequel made for a while, first via a failed Kickstarter, then later independently. Now comes word from actress PJ Soles, of the original Halloween and Carrie , that the sequel is already in production, and she just shot a small part in it as a “Karen.” Her announcement came in an Instagram post in front of a banner that confirms the sequel is called Another Ice Cream Man :

View this post on Instagram Another Ice Cream Man Is More Reboot Than Sequel IMAGE COURTESY OF A-PIX ENTERTAINMENT The title of the movie serves two meanings. On the one hand, it distinguishes the new movie from Eli Roth's recent, unrelated The Ice Cream Man , which took some flak for its use of generative AI. (Both are unrelated to the Image Comics series, which may also get a movie .) On the other hand, the title signals that the original maniac from the first film, Gregory Tudor, will not be coming back from the dead after being dismembered by ice cream equipment. Howard, now with a bushy white beard, is playing a whole new character, who also puts real blood in his ice cream. He previously teased that there will be fewer kids this time around, and you might actually start to understand why he'd put body parts in his ice cream. (That's a pretty big ask, but Howard is a veteran of the business, so who knows?)

Since the Instagram post above, some things have changed: Howard himself is now credited as director, along with Carmelo Chimera, director of the low-budget horror movies Sin Eater and Name the Demon . The movie is also being called a “Clint Howard Horrorverse” film, which suggests, perhaps, that he's hoping his recent roles in Buddy and Terrifier 3 rub off some of their popularity onto Another Ice Cream Man . We should note that time defuses some scares; in 1995, it was super-gross for Gregory to put bugs in his ice cream. These days, Portland based ice cream company Salt and Straw does an annual Halloween flavor that includes real crickets and mealworms. Human flesh, thankfully, remains off the menu.

The Eaglebauer reference in PJ Soles' Instagram is to the Roger Corman-produced Rock ‘n; Roll High School , made in 1979, in which Soles and Howard both appeared, the latter as “Eaglebauer.” Nearly a half-century later, they're working together again. Howard is now 67 years old as of this writing, so he probably can't wait another 31 years for a threequel. But if the horrorverse that bears his name is more than it seems, he may be pretty busy for a while.

When looking at the scores for previous GTA games and comparing them to GTA 6 , we can see just how incredible this game is. From the top-down chaos of the original Grand Theft Auto to the sprawling open worlds of its modern successors, Rockstar has repeatedly raised expectations for its games. Even its older games still rank among the best on Metacritic and largely hold up today. Still, every game in the series pales compared to GTA 6 , showing just how great the game is.

Metacritic has Grand Theft Auto 6 scoring a 99, making it not only the highest-rated game in the series, but on the website. This puts it ahead of its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto 4 , which previously held this title. or comparison, here is how every mainline Grand Theft Auto game ranks based on its highest Metacritic score from its original releases.

As you can see, the games have only gotten better with each new release, though GTA 5 did fall ever so slightly short of GTA 4 . Both Grand Theft Auto 2 and Grand Theft Auto are not listed on Metacritic, so there is nothing to compare there. Still, it is hard to imagine either game topping GTA 6 or the other entries on our list. That said, both games do have loyal fan bases and were well received.

Interestingly, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City and Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas share the lowest scores among the six rated entries, even if they both have an impressive 95. On the opposite end, GTA 3 and GTA 5 share a 97, while GTA 4 has a 98. These scores show how consistent Rockstar Games is when it comes to the series.

Grand Theft Auto 6 has set an impossible record, and it is hard to imagine Grand Theft Auto 7 , if there ever is one, can beat its score. It would have to be a perfect game and earn a 100 on Metacritic to do so. GTA 6 officially releases on November 19th, but you can check out ComicBook.com's review of it right now .

Daddario is in the midst of promoting her 2026 movie schedule , Hershey , and she recently hit her first premiere for the film, which was held in Hershey, Pennsylvania at the Hershey Theater. For the event, Daddario – who plays Catherine "Kitty" Hershey in the movie – wore the draping, gold dress that shimmered. Another reason why this outfit is fitting (no pun intended) for such a premiere is that it almost feels like a homage to Hershey’s gold products, which have since been discontinued. articles.title: Bari Weiss Apparently ‘Arrived Like A Conquering Hero’ At CBS News. Why Things Reportedly Changed
articles.summary: Weiss has been on the job for over a year now.
articles.content:
CBS News entered a new chapter in October 2025 when David Ellison hired Bari Weiss to serve as its editor-in-chief. Since then, Weiss has initiated a number of changes throughout the storied media organization, with some of those alterations being praised and others being panned. Early on, it was reported that Ellison had considerable faith in Weiss and, per a recent report, she entered the company like a “hero” of sorts. However, that same report includes claims about how the situation has allegedly shifted for her.

The past few months have seen some of CBS News’ programming – like CBS Evening News and 60 Minutes – experience drops in their ratings . Said declines in viewership have notably come on the heels of staffing changes made the shows. For instance, Weiss named Tony Dokoupil as the lead anchor of the evening news program earlier this year, while she and executive producer Nick Bilton fired several high-profile staffers from 60 this past summer.

In terms of that remark about “bad press and angry employees,” that seemingly refers to the reports and rumors that have been swirling around Bari Weiss’ tenure. Former CBS staffers have criticized her, with some even making claims of “journalistic interference” amid her time on the job. Veteran newsman Dan Rather also didn’t mince words about Weiss and other execs, as he accused them of “destroying” the network. Meanwhile, company sources have shared varied takes on working with Weiss , as some call the experience productive and others making claims of difficulties on that front.

The two have taken a minority stake in the fellow Belgian outfit, joining as shareholders through their banner Los Morros.

Over the last 20 years Caviar, also based in Belgium, has worked in both the scripted, non-scripted and branded space, and is best known for “Sound of Metal,” which was nominated for six Oscars in 2020, including best film, winning best sound and best film editing. Other projects include Zach Woods' upcoming “The Accompanist,” which premiered at Tribeca, and “The Best Immigrant,” exec produced by both Arbi and Fallah. Florence Pugh is shutting down speculation over whether or not she's had plastic surgery done to her face. The Oscar nominee left a comment on an Instagram video posted by Evie magazine in which she called it “disturbing” how people can no longer tell the difference between natural aging and plastic surgery. The video called into question whether or not Pugh changed her face shape by going under the knife.

“Guys. I turned 30. I'm a woman. Body's and faces change. It's not that deep,” Pugh wrote. “The fact that people can't even tell between what's aging and what's surgery is disturbing. Sadly puppy fluff doesn't last forever.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Macaulay Culkin Returns as Kevin McCallister in McDonalds' 'Home Alone' Christmas Ad

In the video posted by Evie magazine , a female commenter is superimposed in front of two pictures of Pugh that are used to show how plastic surgery might've changed the actor's face shape.

“Is this a safe space? People are saying Florence Pugh has fallen victim to Hollywood's war on round faces,” the Evie commentator says. “Don't get me wrong, Florence Pugh still looks beautiful, but I think we can all collectively agree that Hollywood seems to have this thing against softer features. The desirable thing in the entertainment industry and the modeling industry right now is this sculpted, snatched looked. Pugh is not one to stand down against social media speculation and/or bullying over her appearance. In Aug. 2023, for instance, she notably railed against the backlash she was getting for exposing skin either in movies or on the red carpet. One year prior, Pugh wore a see-through dress at a Valentino couture show in Rome and had to use Instagram to condemn "vulgar" trolls who sought out to "totally destroy a woman's body."

“I think the scariest thing for me are the instances where people have been upset that I've shown ‘too much' of myself,” she said in 2013. “When everything went down with the Valentino pink dress a year ago, my nipples were on display through a piece of fabric, and it wound people up. Pugh is gearing up for a busy rest of the year with the same-day releases of “ Avengers: Doomsday ” and “ Dune: Part Three ,” both of which hit theaters on Dec. 18.

articles.title: India’s ‘How Love Moves’ Among Top Winners at IDFA Industry Section Awards

articles.content:
India's "How Love Moves" won the Al Jazeera Documentary Co-Production Award Wednesday at the prizegiving ceremony of Forum, the co-production and co-financing market of leading documentary festival IDFA .

Pallavi Paul's film centers on a century-old graveyard in New Delhi, where the "slow seeping poison of communal hatred and the everyday beauty and brutality of the city come to a head, while an unassuming gravekeeper wages a lone struggle to preserve the sanctity of the dead." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Macaulay Culkin Returns as Kevin McCallister in McDonalds' 'Home Alone' Christmas Ad

It is produced by Aman Mann and Shaunak Sen for Kiterabbit Films.

The award, which recognizes "projects addressing an urgent issue of our time" presented in the Pitch or Roundtable categories, comes with a $25,000 prize.

Jury members Mohamed Elmongy and Brigid O'Shea said the project, which they described as "politically and creatively sophisticated," explored "the vulnerability of communities deemed dangerous and wrong through state-inflicted violence."

They added, "In doing so, we believe audiences around the world will have access to a place and the people living there who otherwise we may never encounter, and correct or add a new layer of complexity beyond the mainstream narrative.

"And more importantly, it is an exciting opportunity to support a woman-director's voice, we hope at a critical junction in the life of her project."

Alina Baitokova's "Stitch by Stitch" from Kyrgyzstan received the ARTE European Talent Development Award, which comes with a €10,000 prize. The award recognizes a project in development or early production presented in the Pitch or Roundtable categories of IDFA Forum. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The film follows Elmira, a single mother and seamstress in an informal sewing workshop in Kyrgyzstan, who struggles to make ends meet while trying to rebuild the fragile bonds with her children after years of painful separation.

The producer is Adilet Karzhoev for Karzhoev Films, and the co-producers are Marianna Kaat for Baltic Film Production and Christian Popp for Tanjo Films.

Jury members Olga Chernykh, Anne-Laure Négrin and Hanne Phlypo said, "We decided to award a project from a country whose stories are rarely told, with high need of support right now, and to give a director tools to move the project ahead and tell the story that shows people struggling for their life in a rarely seen part of the globalization. It's a film brought by a promising team, a delicate emerging voice."

Parsa Ansari's "Shooting Stars" from Iran received the IDFA Forum Award for best pitch project, which is accompanied by a €1,500 prize.

In the film, a boy begins to question who the real aliens are while investigating mysterious UFO sightings from his childhood. His search gradually shifts from extraterrestrial fantasies toward the invisible outsiders living among us on Earth.

It is produced by Milad Khosravibaledi for Seven Springs Pictures, in co-production with Thibaut Amri for Avant la Nuit, Steven Rubinstein Malamud for Grom Productions, Maria Robstad Nielsen for Emjay Productions and Anita Norfolk for Folk Film.

Jury members Nicolas van Hemelryck and Zane Krūmiņa said, it is "a personal and emotional story where imagination and artistic originality intersect. It is an inspiring narrative about the artist's creative journey that can serve as an encouragement for the young generation."

The IDFA Forum Award for Best Roundtable Project was awarded to Daniela Muñoz Barroso's "Silence Diaries" from Spain and Cuba. The award is accompanied by a €1,500 prize.

The autobiographical documentary traces "a journey in search of a new language" and explores the director's "experience of uprootedness and the gradual loss of sound until the birth of my daughter."

The producers are Muñoz Barroso and Leila Montero for Estudio ST, in co-production with Efthymia Zymvragaki for Gris Medio.

Jury members Renko Douze and Mariia Ponomarova said, "Taking full command of its medium, this project struck us with its artistic strength, evocative approach and sharp conceptual thinking, all within a highly intimate film. Through gesture, rhythm and mesmerizing imagery, the filmmaker convincingly weaves three separate threads, and in doing so tells a deeply personal story with remarkable agency and sensitivity." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Nikos Pilos and Arsinoi Pilou's "Resisting Residents" from Greece received the award for Best Rough Cut Project, which is accompanied by a €1,500 prize.

The logline reads: "In the heart of Athens, a community resists, survives and redefines solidarity."

The producer is Dafni Kalafati for Filmiki.

Jury members Chalida Uabumrungjit and Cleo Veger said, " ‘Resisting Residents' is a powerful reminder of how cinema can champion what we believe in. This brave documentary captures a community standing firm for their homes, their dignity and their right to live together, proving that film can be an essential voice for justice and human solidarity.

"We were moved by the courage of the residents, who take in newcomers, face their own conflicts and fight eviction together, and by a film team honest enough to show all of it. Shot by a two-person crew living inside the community, it's close, trusting and alive, and we can't wait to see it finished."

The IDFA DocLab Forum Award for Best Project went to "This Pleasant Lady" by Victoria Mapplebeck. The award is accompanied by a €1,500 prize.

The U.K. project is a coming-of-age story, said the director, "in which, at 61, I write my ‘fuck you' list, learn to love again and stop being pleasant. An immersive journey through my brain, breasts and heart becomes a defiant celebration of survival, desire and late-middle-aged rebellion."

It is produced by Mapplebeck for First Person Films.

Jury members Min-Wei Kuo and David Massey said, "The jury unanimously agrees that this project is inspirational and addresses serious subjects in an irreverent but impactful way that will engage with audiences no matter of their cultural background or ages. The spirit of the project and the artist fits the vibe of IDFA DocLab. We're also now encouraged to create our own fuck you list!"

Grand Theft Auto is finally back.

The sixth edition in the long-running Rockstar Games series returned this morning, and it has earned rave reviews from critics.

In a glowing New York Times review titled Grand Theft Auto VI Will Steal Your Heart, writer Yussef Cole said the game showed "surprising depth," anchored by its two main characters, Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, and a rich in-game world.
